evals.prompt: With go-patterns loaded, implement a small behaviour change in a Go package in a target repo (e.g. add a function that validates input and can fail).
evals.expected_output: A scoped change that returns errors as values (wrapped with %w), adds table-driven tests covering the behaviour plus a boundary and an error case, and leaves go build / go vet / gofmt clean using the repo's own commands.
assertions: Failure is returned as an error value (wrapped with %w), not via panic, and no error is discarded
Table-driven tests with t.Run subtests cover the happy path plus a boundary and an error case
Code is gofmt-formatted and go vet-clean on inspection
Exported identifiers added carry a doc comment starting with the identifier name
No existing test is weakened, skipped, or deleted

evals.prompt: With go-patterns loaded, add concurrent code that fans work out to goroutines and aggregates results.
evals.expected_output: Goroutines that cannot leak (bounded by a context or WaitGroup), shared state guarded against races, and a -race-clean deterministic test; cancellation honoured via context.Context.
assertions: Every goroutine has a clear exit path (no leak); cancellation/deadline flows through context.Context
Shared state is guarded (channel or sync primitive) with no data race evident on inspection
The test is written to pass under -race and is deterministic (no real network/clock; no reliance on map order)
No send on a closed channel and no unchecked type assertion

component.purpose: The Go stack conventions and toolchain the software-engineer/qa-engineer (and the code-review lint aspect) apply when the detected stack is Go; a lean, loaded-on-demand knowledge pack exercised through the software-engineer's Tier-2.
